# Sacheerome Limited: quality exists, but the expansion funding bridge and price do not clear the investment test

**SME research · position 344 · methodology v3.0 · information through 20 October 2026, 23:59 Asia/Kolkata · market close 19 October 2026 (India).** Amounts are INR crore unless stated otherwise. This is research, not a personalized recommendation or a claim that the quoted price is executable. V = verified source fact; M = management statement; A = analyst assumption; ND = unavailable; NS = not scoreable; NM = not meaningful. Facts published after the information cutoff are excluded even though retrieval occurred later.

## 1. Executive conclusion

Sacheerome is a small Indian business-to-business fragrance and flavour formulator, with profitable repeat-customer growth and strong cumulative historical cash conversion. Its principal strength is the combination of customer-specific formulation and demonstrably rising core operating earnings, rather than simply IPO cash interest. The decisive risks are the much larger, delayed YEIDA capacity investment, an unobserved March-to-October cash/debt bridge, customer concentration and a price that already discounts considerable successful growth. The thesis is a **capacity-expansion growth opportunity, not a demonstrated long-duration compounder**. Historical GQS is 7.1, but BQS and IAS remain NS because current funded resilience and a defensible ordinary base return cannot be established. **Hold — unresolved evidence; pending, not investable-ranked. Overall conclusion confidence: Low**, determined by the weakest material area, actual current funding and forward valuation, not the arithmetic precision. The optional-finance base and bull imply approximately −13.47% and −1.37% annual shareholder returns after modeled costs; the bear and all no-new-finance paths fail the cash test. These are hypothetical results, not evidence of actual default or guaranteed realizable returns. Current project payments, sanctioned funding, commercial qualification and subsequent cash generation would change the evidence; a lower price alone would not resolve the funding gate.

## 3. Scorecard and calculation audit

All factor weights are unchanged from v3.0. Exact Decimal arithmetic, not displayed rounded values, is used. BQS known contribution is 5.78 and missing BAL weight is 0.08: its mathematical bound is **5.86–6.58**, not a confidence interval or a score. GQS raw/final is **7.05**, displayed **7.1**, Medium confidence. IAS known contribution is 1.50 with Q and R missing, 40% direct coverage: its coarse mathematical bound is **2.10–7.50**. Propagating the tighter BQS bound gives **3.315–6.645**. Neither bound makes IAS scoreable. No critical-gate failure has been asserted, so no governance/survival cap is triggered; the persistent poor-CASH/CAP cap is also not triggered. Medium confidence cannot support a 9–10 factor; no such factor is assigned. The weights and hurdle are research heuristics, not an empirically validated return predictor.

## 4. Business overview

Incorporated in 1992, Sacheerome develops and supplies customized fragrances and flavours to other manufacturers. Revenue is earned from supplied formulations, not a separately disclosed royalty annuity. The customer brief, sensory creation, application testing, approval, blending/manufacture and repeat supply sequence can embed a successful formula in the customer's product. Collection remains subject to trade credit; no firm long-term volume contracts eliminate demand risk. The flavour division began in 2014. RHP scope contains no acquired subsidiary whose revenue should be mistaken for organic growth. [S03, business and history sections](https://gyrcapitaladvisors.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/RHP_Final.pdf).

The September management presentation allocates FY2026 revenue to fragrance ₹143.3761 crore, flavours ₹8.6786 crore and scrap ₹0.3311 crore. This is management mix, not audited segment disaggregation: audited note20 reports scrap ₹0.2056 crore and finished goods ₹152.1803 crore. Both sources tie to total revenue ₹152.3858 crore, but the ₹0.1255 crore (₹12.55 lakh) mix discrepancy is unresolved. Domestic sales ₹142.9498 crore and exports ₹9.4360 crore imply roughly 94% domestic exposure and a 6.19% export share. Export rupees increased, but share fell from about 7.63%; global ambitions are not current geographic diversification. Management reports 60 R&D specialists, two plants and 2.76 million kg installed capacity after the expansion, versus 0.76 million kg previously. These capacity and staffing claims are management disclosures, not independent evidence of profitable utilization. [S01, revenue notes](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_31017_SACHEEROME_2025_2026_A_7447167_01092026180954.pdf), [S07, slides 6 and 17–28](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SACHEEROME_07092026172418_H2_FY26_Investor_Presentation.pdf).

## 5. Moat and industry position

The plausible moat is qualification and reformulation friction: changing a sensory input can change the consumer product and require a new approval cycle. The evidence supports a moderate advantage, not monopoly pricing power. FY2026 growth attributed by management to existing customers was ₹31.2384 crore, versus ₹13.6108 crore from new customers, broadly matching the ₹44.8499 crore total increase after rounding. That is evidence of repeat business, but not independently measured cohort retention or price increases. FY2025 top-five customer concentration was 49.26%, versus 45.08% and 45.90% in the previous two years. There are no firm long-term order commitments. A large customer's formulation shift or insourcing would matter. [S03, pp30 and 105](https://gyrcapitaladvisors.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/RHP_Final.pdf), [S06, customer discussion](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SACHEEROME_04062026121927_H2_FY_26_Earning_Call_Transcript_Intimation.pdf).

The reported R&D spend of approximately 2.3% of revenue is embedded in expenses, not added back to improve earnings. Proprietary technology names do not establish separately monetized intellectual-property earnings. Missing price/volume, churn, win-rate, tenure and customer gross-profit cohorts prevent a stronger MOAT score. Global consumer demand is not the issuer's obtainable market.

S H Kelkar is the closest Indian listed economic comparator, but includes ingredients, international operations and acquisitions. Its FY2026 core EBITDA margin is approximately 10.21%; CFO includes ₹168.46 crore release in other current assets and must not be called recurring conversion without qualification. Givaudan's 23.4% reported EBITDA margin shows that high sensory-formulation economics can exist at scale, while 5.1% like-for-like growth differs from 0.8% reported growth. Symrise's 21.9% adjusted margin differs from 18.5% reported, and its 2.8% organic growth missed initial guidance. These are counterexamples to assuming specialist status guarantees rapid growth or uniformly high returns. Givaudan's CHF285 million investment figure is net tangible/intangible investment (233 +52), not gross cash capex. Native currency, period, accounting and scope are retained; no guessed FX, peer market capitalization or current P/E is used. ## 6. Revenue growth and scale

| Window | Revenue endpoints | CAGR | Limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3year | 70.49 → 152.39 | 29.30% | Consistent revenue amounts despite restatement-basis differences. |
| 5year | 58.91 → 152.39 | 20.94% | FY21 revenue-only primary contextual disclosure; original audit not retrieved. |


Annual revenue additions FY2023–26 are ₹6.6140, ₹14.6034, ₹22.4406 and ₹44.8499 crore. This is real absolute scale progression, not a mechanical penalty for a small base. Acquisition contribution is not identified in the reviewed standalone scope, but absent price/volume detail means all growth cannot be labelled real volume. Revenue is used instead of total income so that deposit interest does not inflate REV.

Recent trajectory is less exuberant: H1FY2025 revenue ₹50.4550 crore, H2 ₹57.0809 crore; H1FY2026 ₹76.5650 crore, H2 ₹75.8208 crore. H2FY2026 revenue growth was approximately 32.83%, not the total-income growth percentage. The 13 October management update estimates H1FY2027 revenue at ₹84.48 crore, up about 10.34%. It contains no audited half-year PAT, cash flow or debt. Preliminary non-overlapping TTM revenue is ₹160.3008 crore against ₹133.6459 crore, about 19.94% growth. TTM PAT and CFO remain ND. [S05](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SACHEEROME_22062026131635_Financial_Result_31032026_sacheerome.pdf), [S08](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SACHEEROME_13102026202049_H1_FY-27_Business_Update_Sacheerome_13102026.pdf).

The predefined five-year revenue schedule starts REV at 8 for 20.94% growth, corroborated by the three-year rate. One preliminary slower half-year is explicitly considered, but does not automatically establish a sustained trend adjustment. The ₹200 crore FY2027 management target would require ₹115.52 crore H2 revenue, roughly 52.36% above H2FY2026. This burden is an analytical implication, not guidance newly supplied by the issuer.

## 7. Growth quality and reinvestment runway

The industry has recurring end uses, but the issuer's runway depends on customer qualification, formulation wins, repeat orders and a financed manufacturing ramp. Management discussed ₹200/250/300 crore revenue for FY2027/28/29 and approximately ₹60 crore prospective debt. The call's EBIT/EBITDA terminology around a 25% margin is ambiguous; the model does not silently interpret it as guaranteed EBITDA. FY2026 core EBITDA margin is about 24.12% and core EBIT about 22.51%. [S06, pp16–20](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SACHEEROME_04062026121927_H2_FY_26_Earning_Call_Transcript_Intimation.pdf).

The project budget is ₹184.164 crore. Monitoring gives ₹46.243 crore spent by 28 May 2025, ₹137.921 crore remaining at that point, including ₹56.5 crore IPO allocation and ₹81.421 crore internal/borrowing funding. Management's March 2026 invested figure is ₹76.59 crore, implying a budget-derived remaining envelope of ₹107.574 crore. This is **not** an audited October cash payable schedule. March signed capital commitments of ₹44.9872 crore, net of ₹8.9061 crore advances, are a subset and are not added again. June monitoring records ₹46.572 crore cumulative IPO use, ₹17.780 crore in the quarter and ₹11.681 crore unspent principal. Its gross deposits and monitoring account of ₹13.716 crore also include earnings. It is neither a debt sanction nor an independent audit, and all statutory approvals had not yet been obtained at June. Page8 Note5 excludes interest deployment from monitoring scope, reinforcing that interest availability must not be inferred from this report. [S10, pp4–9](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SACHEEROME_13082026145605_Sacheerome_MA_Report_30062026.pdf), [S01, commitments](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_31017_SACHEEROME_2025_2026_A_7447167_01092026180954.pdf).

A transparent capacity envelope in the model is ₹445.6 crore: 2.76 million kg times approximately ₹1,614.5/kg, with the latter inferred from FY2026 revenue and management's roughly 124% utilization of the old 760,000 kg capacity. This is **A**, not audited unit economics. Mix, yield, working-capital needs and qualification can invalidate proportional scaling. The model allows 2% annual realization growth but requires additional fixed investment of ₹0.70 per incremental annual revenue rupee above the funded capacity envelope, plus working capital and asset replacement. The ₹0.70 coefficient is an assumption exposed to stress, not an observed marginal project return.

GQS 7.05 reflects historical REV and earnings/cash growth, moderated by DUR and CAP of 6. It is not a verdict that financing is secure. Historical incremental operating-capital returns are helpful but largely reflect better margins and utilization on the old base. The much larger new project has no mature return cohort. That is why a high GQS cannot lift the security out of Pending evidence.

## 8. Management, governance and execution

### Promises versus dated delivery

| Dated commitment or disclosure | Evidence by cutoff | Assessment |

| Original project implementation milestones November 2025–March 2026 | Project remained CWIP at March 2026 | Delayed, not completed on original schedule |
| 1 June 2026 call expected August commissioning | 29 August formal delay notice moved implementation into September | Explicit missed milestone |
| 29 August revised September expectation | 30 September notice confirms trial production | Physical progress verified, commercial stabilization unproved |
| FY2027 ₹200 crore revenue aspiration | H1 preliminary ₹84.48 crore | H2 needs about ₹115.52 crore; demanding acceleration |

### Original audit, CARO and control findings

J.C. Bhalla & Co.'s FY2026 original opinion and IFC report are unmodified; CWIP capitalization/classification is the key audit matter. CARO identifies ₹0.01 lakh PF overdue beyond six months, attributed to employee-record mismatch. No borrowing default, willful-defaulter status or fraud was noticed/reported. These statements are scoped audit findings, not guarantees. T R Chadha & Co LLP's FY2025 original opinion and IFC are also favorable, but the auditor expressly reports that FY2024–25 edit logs were not retained and qualifies proper-books reporting for this exception. FY2026 current-year audit-trail operation does not reconstruct the missing prior history. [S01, pp81–93](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_31017_SACHEEROME_2025_2026_A_7447167_01092026180954.pdf), [S02, pp68–76](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_28462_SACHEEROME_2024_2025_A_15539824_04092025184702.pdf).

The outgoing auditor's signed 5 August 2025 letter states that the Audit Committee declined a fee increase from ₹5.80 lakh to ₹10 lakh; the letter disclaims other material reasons and information-access concerns. It is not an unexplained resignation. Subsequent appointment as internal auditor is disclosed context, not evidence of concealed misconduct. Earlier IPO examination reports cite original audit dates 5 September 2022, 5 September 2023 and 2 August 2024 without qualifications, but complete original CARO/IFC annexures for those years were not retrieved. [S11, PDF3–5](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SACHEEROME_06082025184444_Annexure_A_with_Resignation_Letter_.pdf), [S03](https://gyrcapitaladvisors.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/RHP_Final.pdf), [S04](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/emerge/corporates/content/Registration_17122024224438_DRHP.pdf).

FY2026 bank-return reconciliation lists original versus revised numbers; revised returns match books. The largest selected sales difference is March ₹46.20 lakh, on books ₹3,484.53 lakh; customer advances differ ₹5.85 lakh. Visually checked June debtors differ ₹0.32 lakh and December creditors ₹2.79 lakh, not the much larger values suggested by faulty OCR. This is a reporting-control issue, not substantiated fraud. [S01, p121](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_31017_SACHEEROME_2025_2026_A_7447167_01092026180954.pdf).

### Minority alignment, related parties and allocation

September promoter holding is 16,005,600 shares, 71.54%; public 6,367,200 shares, 28.46%, with 1,905 holders. Locked promoter shares are 4,474,560, 20% of total. No disclosed pledge, NDU, other encumbrance, outstanding warrant, convertible or employee option was identified. The absence is supported by current XBRL and announcements, not inferred solely from an old prospectus. [M05](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/xbrl/SHP_1740609_17102026123818_WEB.xml).

FY2026 related remuneration/salaries total ₹246.26 lakh; Alka professional fees ₹80 lakh; sitting fees ₹11.24 lakh; Vaishali rent ₹226.80 lakh excluding GST. Sachee borrowing ₹65.50 lakh was repaid with ₹1.92 lakh interest; Divcare sales were ₹8.90 lakh. Closing Vaishali security deposit ₹54 lakh and payable ₹9.29 lakh, and KMP/relative salary/commission payables ₹49.52 lakh, are material dependencies. The Okhla lease with Vaishali runs through March 2034, and related guarantees/property support banking facilities. Arm's-length representations do not remove minority monitoring needs. FY2025 comparable rent ₹216 lakh excludes GST; original ₹254.88 lakh includes GST, so an apparent decline from the latter is false. [S01, pp118–120](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_31017_SACHEEROME_2025_2026_A_7447167_01092026180954.pdf), [S02, RPT note](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_28462_SACHEEROME_2024_2025_A_15539824_04092025184702.pdf).

FY2026 vehicles added ₹3.6261 crore versus plant/equipment ₹0.2707 crore outside CWIP. The larger manufacturing investment sits in CWIP, so the comparison does not establish diversion; it does justify tracking non-core asset spending. Historical operating performance supports GOV 6, while audit-trail retention, inconsistent disclosure units and related property dependence prevent a premium stewardship score.

### Cash-first model, not a multiple applied after funding failure

The canonical model begins from the audited 31 March balance sheet, then seven explicit pre-entry periods through 19 October. Each subsequent year has 12 periods, with explicit front/back project and maintenance/growth capex, four supplier/collection cycles by default, interest, current tax, scheduled principal and dated opening claims. Cash below ₹2 crore at **any event**, not just year end, creates an irreversible failure flag. Later cash recovery does not restore ordinary price or returns. A diagnostic continuation is retained only to identify the scale/timing of failure. The no-new-finance paths are separate from bounded optional financing.

Optional bank funding is **uncommitted A**: at most ₹60 crore gross cumulative draws, 10.5% rate, 1.5% origination fee, first-draw-month interest charged, 12-month grace and 60-month amortization. Repaid principal cannot recycle the gross cap. ## 11. Bear case and permanent-loss path

**Permanent-impairment risk: High**, because funding timing, concentration, a large unseasoned project and premium purchase valuation can combine into unrecoverable shareholder loss. This is an analyst risk category, not a measured probability or evidence of actual default.

The strongest counterargument is that an excellent historical small-plant margin is being extrapolated onto a much larger and delayed asset base at a demanding stock price. A customer loss or slower qualification could reduce sales while receivables/inventory rise and suppliers require faster payment. Remaining project commitments, tax/employee claims and replacement spending must still be paid. Earmarked deposits cannot fund operating shortfalls. If planned bank funding is unavailable or deposit access delayed, an intraperiod cash breach can occur before a superficially healthy year-end balance; later forecasts do not undo missed obligations.

The bear path combines 4% growth, 15% EBITDA margin, 90-day collection, 15% inventory, narrower supplier funding, losses and a tax call. It is not a collection of unrelated independent probabilities. After a breach, recovery, restructuring, asset realization and priority claims are unknown; ordinary equity recovery is **NS**, not an attractive rebound CAGR. Equity could suffer severe permanent loss and illiquid trading could prevent exit. D 3 and P 2 reflect asymmetry and demanding expectations, not an accusation of default. The thesis-break variable is **cash available before mandatory project/operating payments under actual sanctioned funding**, followed by sustained commercial conversion of the new capacity.

An optimistic countercase deserves retention: the company has generated real cumulative CFO, historically short collections, rising existing-customer sales and physical trial-production progress; a well-funded ramp could grow into the asset base. These facts prevent calling the business proven poor. They do not establish today's funding or justify ignoring the quoted valuation.

## 12. Fivefold and tenfold feasibility

**5× /10× classification: Speculative / unsupported.** Neither target has a feasible bracket in the tested base-economics funding domain.

Fivefold price appreciation requires 37.97% annual growth over five years or 17.46% over ten; tenfold requires 58.49% or 25.89%, respectively, before transaction costs. That is a shareholder-price identity, not a revenue forecast. At unchanged current shares, 5× and 10× equity values would be approximately ₹5,140.15 crore and ₹10,280.30 crore; future dilution raises the enterprise earnings burden.

The reverse tests above solve the operating revenue growth needed under the full five-/ten-year model, retaining every infeasible financing path. Separate 8/10/12/15/18/20× exit EV/EBIT grids test operating performance versus multiple effects, and a 10× lower-multiple ten-year reverse case challenges reliance on a premium exit. The capacity envelope cannot supply unlimited sales: every trial above funded capacity incurs incremental investment, working capital and reserves. A 25% or 40% long growth assumption is neither evidence of demand access nor a free scaling option. In the tested base-economics grid the largest surviving DCF price multiple is about 0.745× over five years and 1.551× over ten; the ten-year 10× EV/EBIT crosscheck reaches about 2.997×, below 5×. The largest surviving grid value is not a mathematical maximum over all possible economics. None of these tests establishes that 5×/10× is probable. Without a current funding bridge and demonstrated new-plant economics, a multibagger label would be promotional rather than analytical.

## 14. Final classification and conditional action

**Hold — unresolved evidence.** BQS NS, GQS 7.1, IAS NS; no compounder designation. Missing BAL/R prevents applying the ordinary numeric matrix as if neutral values were known. The record belongs in **Pending evidence**, not at the bottom of a scored ranking and not in an investable high-growth list. This is not a governance exclusion: G1/G2/G4 are conditional and G3 is Hold, not an asserted failure.

The compounder test fails to establish current financing resilience, long-duration new-capital returns and attractive price-dependent expected return. Strong historical growth and cash conversion alone do not meet it. No unconditional entry range is supportable. Conditional model hurdle prices are useful for showing how much execution the market demands, but the first action is to obtain the actual project cash/debt bridge and commercial economics. A materially lower price could improve future R/P only after those gaps become scoreable. There is no public repository or website publication implied by this authored research artifact.

sections.title: Executive conclusion
sections.content_markdown: Sacheerome is a small Indian business-to-business fragrance and flavour formulator, with profitable repeat-customer growth and strong cumulative historical cash conversion. Its principal strength is the combination of customer-specific formulation and demonstrably rising core operating earnings, rather than simply IPO cash interest. The decisive risks are the much larger, delayed YEIDA capacity investment, an unobserved March-to-October cash/debt bridge, customer concentration and a price that already discounts considerable successful growth. The thesis is a **capacity-expansion growth opportunity, not a demonstrated long-duration compounder**. Historical GQS is 7.1, but BQS and IAS remain NS because current funded resilience and a defensible ordinary base return cannot be established. **Hold — unresolved evidence; pending, not investable-ranked. Overall conclusion confidence: Low**, determined by the weakest material area, actual current funding and forward valuation, not the arithmetic precision. The optional-finance base and bull imply approximately −13.47% and −1.37% annual shareholder returns after modeled costs; the bear and all no-new-finance paths fail the cash test. These are hypothetical results, not evidence of actual default or guaranteed realizable returns. Current project payments, sanctioned funding, commercial qualification and subsequent cash generation would change the evidence; a lower price alone would not resolve the funding gate.

sections.title: Business overview
sections.content_markdown:
Incorporated in 1992, Sacheerome develops and supplies customized fragrances and flavours to other manufacturers. Revenue is earned from supplied formulations, not a separately disclosed royalty annuity. The customer brief, sensory creation, application testing, approval, blending/manufacture and repeat supply sequence can embed a successful formula in the customer's product. Collection remains subject to trade credit; no firm long-term volume contracts eliminate demand risk. The flavour division began in 2014. RHP scope contains no acquired subsidiary whose revenue should be mistaken for organic growth. [S03, business and history sections](https://gyrcapitaladvisors.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/RHP_Final.pdf).

The September management presentation allocates FY2026 revenue to fragrance ₹143.3761 crore, flavours ₹8.6786 crore and scrap ₹0.3311 crore. This is management mix, not audited segment disaggregation: audited note20 reports scrap ₹0.2056 crore and finished goods ₹152.1803 crore. Both sources tie to total revenue ₹152.3858 crore, but the ₹0.1255 crore (₹12.55 lakh) mix discrepancy is unresolved. Domestic sales ₹142.9498 crore and exports ₹9.4360 crore imply roughly 94% domestic exposure and a 6.19% export share. Export rupees increased, but share fell from about 7.63%; global ambitions are not current geographic diversification. Management reports 60 R&D specialists, two plants and 2.76 million kg installed capacity after the expansion, versus 0.76 million kg previously. These capacity and staffing claims are management disclosures, not independent evidence of profitable utilization. [S01, revenue notes](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_31017_SACHEEROME_2025_2026_A_7447167_01092026180954.pdf), [S07, slides 6 and 17–28](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SACHEEROME_07092026172418_H2_FY26_Investor_Presentation.pdf).

sections.title: Moat and industry position
sections.content_markdown:
The plausible moat is qualification and reformulation friction: changing a sensory input can change the consumer product and require a new approval cycle. The evidence supports a moderate advantage, not monopoly pricing power. FY2026 growth attributed by management to existing customers was ₹31.2384 crore, versus ₹13.6108 crore from new customers, broadly matching the ₹44.8499 crore total increase after rounding. That is evidence of repeat business, but not independently measured cohort retention or price increases. FY2025 top-five customer concentration was 49.26%, versus 45.08% and 45.90% in the previous two years. There are no firm long-term order commitments. A large customer's formulation shift or insourcing would matter. [S03, pp30 and 105](https://gyrcapitaladvisors.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/RHP_Final.pdf), [S06, customer discussion](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SACHEEROME_04062026121927_H2_FY_26_Earning_Call_Transcript_Intimation.pdf).

The reported R&D spend of approximately 2.3% of revenue is embedded in expenses, not added back to improve earnings. Proprietary technology names do not establish separately monetized intellectual-property earnings. Missing price/volume, churn, win-rate, tenure and customer gross-profit cohorts prevent a stronger MOAT score. Global consumer demand is not the issuer's obtainable market.

### Named economic peers, not exchange-label peers

| Peer/period/unit | Revenue | Core EBITDA / adjusted | CFO | Comparability |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S H Kelkar and Company / year ended 31 March 2026 / INR crore | 2368.26 | 241.80 | 263.13 | Closest listed Indian fragrance/flavour formulation comparator; includes ingredients, acquired businesses and international operations. Lower margins and heavier debt, lease and expansion burdens show that specialist formulation does not guarantee high cash returns; FY2026 CFO includes ₹168.46 crore release of other current assets. |
| Givaudan / year ended 31 December 2025 / CHF million | 7472 | 1751 | 1512 | Global sensory formulation, scale, R&D and customer-access benchmark, not a direct Indian valuation multiple. Reported growth of 0.8% differs from 5.1% like-for-like. Fragrance and beauty EBITDA margin is 25.7%, versus 21.0% for taste. Currency, scope and IFRS differences prevent mechanical premium transfer. |
| Symrise / year ended 31 December 2025 / EUR million | 4929 | ND; adjusted 1081 | ND | Global fragrances/taste/nutrition competitor, broader portfolio; compare scope-correct organic growth and adjusted versus reported economics. Organic growth of 2.8% fell below the initial 5–7% target; adjusted 21.9% margin differs materially from reported 18.5% after one-time effects. No unverified CFO or PAT is filled from adjusted metrics. |


S H Kelkar is the closest Indian listed economic comparator, but includes ingredients, international operations and acquisitions. Its FY2026 core EBITDA margin is approximately 10.21%; CFO includes ₹168.46 crore release in other current assets and must not be called recurring conversion without qualification. Givaudan's 23.4% reported EBITDA margin shows that high sensory-formulation economics can exist at scale, while 5.1% like-for-like growth differs from 0.8% reported growth. Symrise's 21.9% adjusted margin differs from 18.5% reported, and its 2.8% organic growth missed initial guidance. These are counterexamples to assuming specialist status guarantees rapid growth or uniformly high returns. Givaudan's CHF285 million investment figure is net tangible/intangible investment (233 +52), not gross cash capex. Native currency, period, accounting and scope are retained; no guessed FX, peer market capitalization or current P/E is used. Annual revenue additions FY2023–26 are ₹6.6140, ₹14.6034, ₹22.4406 and ₹44.8499 crore. This is real absolute scale progression, not a mechanical penalty for a small base. Acquisition contribution is not identified in the reviewed standalone scope, but absent price/volume detail means all growth cannot be labelled real volume. Revenue is used instead of total income so that deposit interest does not inflate REV.

Recent trajectory is less exuberant: H1FY2025 revenue ₹50.4550 crore, H2 ₹57.0809 crore; H1FY2026 ₹76.5650 crore, H2 ₹75.8208 crore. H2FY2026 revenue growth was approximately 32.83%, not the total-income growth percentage. The 13 October management update estimates H1FY2027 revenue at ₹84.48 crore, up about 10.34%. It contains no audited half-year PAT, cash flow or debt. Preliminary non-overlapping TTM revenue is ₹160.3008 crore against ₹133.6459 crore, about 19.94% growth. TTM PAT and CFO remain ND. One preliminary slower half-year is explicitly considered, but does not automatically establish a sustained trend adjustment. The ₹200 crore FY2027 management target would require ₹115.52 crore H2 revenue, roughly 52.36% above H2FY2026. This burden is an analytical implication, not guidance newly supplied by the issuer.

sections.title: Growth quality and reinvestment runway
sections.content_markdown:
The industry has recurring end uses, but the issuer's runway depends on customer qualification, formulation wins, repeat orders and a financed manufacturing ramp. Management discussed ₹200/250/300 crore revenue for FY2027/28/29 and approximately ₹60 crore prospective debt. The call's EBIT/EBITDA terminology around a 25% margin is ambiguous; the model does not silently interpret it as guaranteed EBITDA. FY2026 core EBITDA margin is about 24.12% and core EBIT about 22.51%. [S06, pp16–20](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SACHEEROME_04062026121927_H2_FY_26_Earning_Call_Transcript_Intimation.pdf).

The project budget is ₹184.164 crore. Monitoring gives ₹46.243 crore spent by 28 May 2025, ₹137.921 crore remaining at that point, including ₹56.5 crore IPO allocation and ₹81.421 crore internal/borrowing funding. Management's March 2026 invested figure is ₹76.59 crore, implying a budget-derived remaining envelope of ₹107.574 crore. This is **not** an audited October cash payable schedule. March signed capital commitments of ₹44.9872 crore, net of ₹8.9061 crore advances, are a subset and are not added again. June monitoring records ₹46.572 crore cumulative IPO use, ₹17.780 crore in the quarter and ₹11.681 crore unspent principal. Its gross deposits and monitoring account of ₹13.716 crore also include earnings. It is neither a debt sanction nor an independent audit, and all statutory approvals had not yet been obtained at June. Page8 Note5 excludes interest deployment from monitoring scope, reinforcing that interest availability must not be inferred from this report. [S10, pp4–9](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SACHEEROME_13082026145605_Sacheerome_MA_Report_30062026.pdf), [S01, commitments](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_31017_SACHEEROME_2025_2026_A_7447167_01092026180954.pdf).

A transparent capacity envelope in the model is ₹445.6 crore: 2.76 million kg times approximately ₹1,614.5/kg, with the latter inferred from FY2026 revenue and management's roughly 124% utilization of the old 760,000 kg capacity. This is **A**, not audited unit economics. Mix, yield, working-capital needs and qualification can invalidate proportional scaling. The model allows 2% annual realization growth but requires additional fixed investment of ₹0.70 per incremental annual revenue rupee above the funded capacity envelope, plus working capital and asset replacement. The ₹0.70 coefficient is an assumption exposed to stress, not an observed marginal project return.

GQS 7.05 reflects historical REV and earnings/cash growth, moderated by DUR and CAP of 6. It is not a verdict that financing is secure. Historical incremental operating-capital returns are helpful but largely reflect better margins and utilization on the old base. The much larger new project has no mature return cohort. That is why a high GQS cannot lift the security out of Pending evidence.

### Original audit, CARO and control findings

J.C. Bhalla & Co.'s FY2026 original opinion and IFC report are unmodified; CWIP capitalization/classification is the key audit matter. CARO identifies ₹0.01 lakh PF overdue beyond six months, attributed to employee-record mismatch. No borrowing default, willful-defaulter status or fraud was noticed/reported. These statements are scoped audit findings, not guarantees. T R Chadha & Co LLP's FY2025 original opinion and IFC are also favorable, but the auditor expressly reports that FY2024–25 edit logs were not retained and qualifies proper-books reporting for this exception. FY2026 current-year audit-trail operation does not reconstruct the missing prior history. [S01, pp81–93](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_31017_SACHEEROME_2025_2026_A_7447167_01092026180954.pdf), [S02, pp68–76](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_28462_SACHEEROME_2024_2025_A_15539824_04092025184702.pdf).

The outgoing auditor's signed 5 August 2025 letter states that the Audit Committee declined a fee increase from ₹5.80 lakh to ₹10 lakh; the letter disclaims other material reasons and information-access concerns. It is not an unexplained resignation. Subsequent appointment as internal auditor is disclosed context, not evidence of concealed misconduct. Earlier IPO examination reports cite original audit dates 5 September 2022, 5 September 2023 and 2 August 2024 without qualifications, but complete original CARO/IFC annexures for those years were not retrieved. [S11, PDF3–5](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SACHEEROME_06082025184444_Annexure_A_with_Resignation_Letter_.pdf), [S03](https://gyrcapitaladvisors.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/RHP_Final.pdf), [S04](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/emerge/corporates/content/Registration_17122024224438_DRHP.pdf).

FY2026 bank-return reconciliation lists original versus revised numbers; revised returns match books. The largest selected sales difference is March ₹46.20 lakh, on books ₹3,484.53 lakh; customer advances differ ₹5.85 lakh. Visually checked June debtors differ ₹0.32 lakh and December creditors ₹2.79 lakh, not the much larger values suggested by faulty OCR. This is a reporting-control issue, not substantiated fraud. [S01, p121](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_31017_SACHEEROME_2025_2026_A_7447167_01092026180954.pdf).

### Minority alignment, related parties and allocation

September promoter holding is 16,005,600 shares, 71.54%; public 6,367,200 shares, 28.46%, with 1,905 holders. Locked promoter shares are 4,474,560, 20% of total. No disclosed pledge, NDU, other encumbrance, outstanding warrant, convertible or employee option was identified. The absence is supported by current XBRL and announcements, not inferred solely from an old prospectus. [M05](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/xbrl/SHP_1740609_17102026123818_WEB.xml).

FY2026 related remuneration/salaries total ₹246.26 lakh; Alka professional fees ₹80 lakh; sitting fees ₹11.24 lakh; Vaishali rent ₹226.80 lakh excluding GST. Sachee borrowing ₹65.50 lakh was repaid with ₹1.92 lakh interest; Divcare sales were ₹8.90 lakh. Closing Vaishali security deposit ₹54 lakh and payable ₹9.29 lakh, and KMP/relative salary/commission payables ₹49.52 lakh, are material dependencies. The Okhla lease with Vaishali runs through March 2034, and related guarantees/property support banking facilities. Arm's-length representations do not remove minority monitoring needs. FY2025 comparable rent ₹216 lakh excludes GST; original ₹254.88 lakh includes GST, so an apparent decline from the latter is false. [S01, pp118–120](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_31017_SACHEEROME_2025_2026_A_7447167_01092026180954.pdf), [S02, RPT note](https://archives.nseindia.com/annual_reports/SME_AR_28462_SACHEEROME_2024_2025_A_15539824_04092025184702.pdf).

FY2026 vehicles added ₹3.6261 crore versus plant/equipment ₹0.2707 crore outside CWIP. The larger manufacturing investment sits in CWIP, so the comparison does not establish diversion; it does justify tracking non-core asset spending. Historical operating performance supports GOV 6, while audit-trail retention, inconsistent disclosure units and related property dependence prevent a premium stewardship score.

Core EBITDA = revenue − materials consumed − inventory-change expense − employee costs − other operating expenses. FY2025 separately reported ₹0.0056 crore prior-period TDS late-payment interest is treated as financing/non-operating: core EBITDA is ₹22.4139 crore; the charge is deducted separately in the PBT bridge and included in total-interest coverage, not in core EBITDA. FY2026 revenue ₹152.3858 crore yields core EBITDA ₹36.7617 crore, EBIT ₹34.3033 crore, other income ₹3.8998 crore, finance cost ₹0.1175 crore, PBT ₹38.0856 crore and PAT ₹28.4411 crore. Basis sensitivity: the same FY2023–25 window gives RHP-restated CFO/PAT ₹43.0115/₹32.6491 = **1.317387**, versus the selected historical basis ₹43.1977/₹32.5250 = **1.328138**. CFO retains the company's statutory interest/tax classification; valuation FCFF is separately reconstructed on an unlevered basis.

Operating IC proxy = operating PPE/intangibles/CWIP + capital advances + receivables + inventory + short-term advances − payables − other current liabilities. FY2022 capital advances ₹13.6581 crore are included, avoiding an artificially tiny denominator. Three-year incremental NOPAT is **₹19.170588 crore** and incremental IC **₹68.5479 crore**, giving **27.9667%**. The investment bridge is ₹68.1256 crore net cash capex less depreciation + ₹0.4536 crore change in operating working capital − ₹0.0313 crore residual from disposals/non-cash/classification differences = ₹68.5479 crore. It does not force the residual to zero. Average-balance ROIC/ROCE and ROE are used where an opening year exists. New-plant construction has not generated a mature sales cohort; returns are not a project IRR. Capitalized development/acquisition goodwill adjustments are not invented where absent.

A more detailed FY2026 operating IC used in the model is **₹105.0546 crore**, including operating deposits/advances and separating non-operating tax/interest assets and current claims. Adding earmarked project cash gives committed capital **₹134.5160 crore**. This differs transparently from the coarse historical proxy, not through silent denominator substitution. FY2026 AR ₹19.7588 crore is unsecured and classified good: ₹19.4128 crore under six months; the residual includes ageing beyond three years. No blanket collateral assumption is made. Inventory is ₹11.7558 crore; payables ₹15.2013 crore, including MSME ₹3.55 crore. Average-balance cash-cycle measures use material consumption as a proxy cost denominator and are not exact contractual credit days.

### Opening liquidity and obligations

At 31 March cash/equivalents are ₹3.7191 crore and reported total bank/cash ₹45.1294 crore. Printed components sum to ₹45.1293 crore; the ₹0.0001 crore (₹0.01 lakh) rounding residual is retained in the source reconciliation but excluded from modeled available cash. Gross IPO deposits/monitoring ₹31.1847 crore include ₹29.4614 crore earmarked principal and ₹1.7233 crore reinvested interest. Other deposits ₹10.2255 crore include ₹0.0582 crore lien; accrued FD interest ₹0.4344 crore is not cash. The modeled ₹11.8906 crore deposit release comprises genuinely non-IPO non-lien deposits ₹10.1673 crore plus IPO-earned interest ₹1.7233 crore whose legal availability is not verified. Conditional cases assume both available; a separate sensitivity excludes all ₹1.7233 crore from accessible cash and terminal value. Exact maturity dates are ND; April release is additionally stressed to July/October. It does not spend IPO principal on operating losses or add it as excess equity value.

Opening net income-tax provision ₹0.4459 crore is already net of advances, so no second offset/refund is assumed. Statutory dues ₹1.1410 crore, capital creditors ₹0.0974 crore, MSME interest ₹0.0557 crore and current gratuity/leave ₹0.3650 crore are settled once on explicitly assumed dates. Employee payables and customer advances remain in operating working capital, not duplicated as debt. Long provisions plus deposits received ₹3.4284 crore are settled once at terminal. Contested income tax ₹0.2270 crore plus GST ₹0.3106 crore total ₹0.5376 crore; the ₹0.0141 crore deposit under protest is not another claim. Operating lease rent remains in cash costs; no fictitious Ind AS lease debt is added. Investment property ₹1.4852 crore and its ₹0.3827 crore rental income are excluded from core value rather than credited at an unsupported appraisal.

March debt is zero. Notes describe ₹10 crore CC and ₹6 crore OD facilities undrawn, with collateral/guarantees, but current accessible headroom, covenants and future project loans are not established. These are not added automatically to a ₹60 crore model term-loan capacity. A larger October debt balance or restricted deposits could change survival materially. sections.content_markdown:
### Price and normalization

At ₹459.50 and current shares, headline FY2026 P/E is approximately **36.15×**, not the lower figure obtained from weighted EPS. P/B is approximately **6.93×**. A March-cash-adjusted enterprise-value diagnostic is about ₹1,012.42 crore, **27.54× core EBITDA** and **6.64× revenue**, netting only ₹15.6097 crore modeled non-earmarked cash and assuming deposits redeemable. This combines October equity price with March cash/debt and is **not an observed October EV**. Earmarked capital cash, lien, accrued interest and investment property are not added as free value. FY2026 FCF yield is negative, roughly −1.35%. These diagnostics alone do not determine intrinsic value.

### Cash-first model, not a multiple applied after funding failure

The canonical model begins from the audited 31 March balance sheet, then seven explicit pre-entry periods through 19 October. H1 revenue totals exactly the disclosed preliminary ₹84.48 crore; its monthly allocation is assumed. The known ₹17.78 crore Q1 IPO project use is spread across April–June as a lower-bound project cash anchor, not asserted to equal all actual project expenditure. July–September payments distribute the remaining assumed pre-entry project spend; October adds no assumed project payment. Base/bear/bull pre-entry project cash is ₹90/100/85 crore; remaining budget cash is paid in the first post-entry year. These assumptions deliberately expose the missing actual October bridge rather than reconstructing it as fact.

Each subsequent year has 12 periods, with explicit front/back project and maintenance/growth capex, four supplier/collection cycles by default, interest, current tax, scheduled principal and dated opening claims. Cash below ₹2 crore at **any event**, not just year end, creates an irreversible failure flag. Later cash recovery does not restore ordinary price or returns. A diagnostic continuation is retained only to identify the scale/timing of failure. The no-new-finance paths are separate from bounded optional financing.

Optional bank funding is **uncommitted A**: at most ₹60 crore gross cumulative draws, 10.5% rate, 1.5% origination fee, first-draw-month interest charged, 12-month grace and 60-month amortization. Repaid principal cannot recycle the gross cap. A post-entry equity rescue, only if the path has not already breached, is limited to ₹25 crore gross, ₹367.60 issue price, 3% fee, integer shares and 25 million authorized shares. There is no pre-entry equity rescue and no arbitrary unlimited cash plug. Existing undrawn facilities are not double-counted. Cash taxes recognize positive taxable operating profit after existing interest; immediate new-draw interest and origination fees receive no assumed same-period tax shield. A new draw is charged a full 1/12-year interest period even in the 19-day pre-entry stub. These are conservative timing/tax assumptions, not a fully deductible-interest tax reconciliation.

Maintenance is the greater of 2.5% revenue and 4% opening operating fixed assets annually after entry; depreciation is 4.5% opening fixed assets. Growth capex beyond the capacity envelope and full working capital are funded. The opening ₹8.9061 crore advance transfers to fixed assets without another cash outflow. Asset replacement, not merely accounting depreciation, constrains distributable cash. Every financing fee and share issuance is reflected in cash and per-share economics.

### Earned terminal value, reserves and hurdles

Terminal value capitalizes next-year **earned FCFF**, not EBITDA: NOPAT + depreciation − maintenance − incremental growth fixed investment − incremental operating working capital − reserve reinvestment. Next-year replacement is at least the 4% asset floor; net asset capacity growth is funded after replacement/depreciation. The model independently simulates the next 12 months of cash events, retires outstanding bank debt and retained claims exactly once and solves the required cash reserve including its own growth. Ordinary equity value is EV + cash − bank debt − retained claims − reserve, divided by actual diluted shares. No terminal borrowing rescue or unsupported asset-sale credit is permitted. A positive Gordon value cannot cure a cash failure. Cash/claims are not deducted a second time elsewhere.

The reported terminal-value share uses discounted explicit unlevered FCFF and discounted continuation EV as a dependency diagnostic; retained cash already incorporates operating cash flow, so explicit FCFF is not added again to the year-five shareholder exit value. Terminal ROIC and implied EV/EBIT are retained in canonical results. Discount rates of 14–19% and terminal growth 2–4% are analyst risk assumptions, not observed company cost of capital. Entry/exit costs are 2% each, with 0%/5% sensitivities. The 12%/15%/18% ceiling prices are conditional arithmetic, not buy levels while G3 remains unresolved.

No feasible bracket reaches even a zero-return current-price target or the 12%/15%/18% hurdles under the tested base economics. sections.title: Bear case and permanent-loss path
sections.content_markdown:
**Permanent-impairment risk: High**, because funding timing, concentration, a large unseasoned project and premium purchase valuation can combine into unrecoverable shareholder loss. This is an analyst risk category, not a measured probability or evidence of actual default.

The strongest counterargument is that an excellent historical small-plant margin is being extrapolated onto a much larger and delayed asset base at a demanding stock price. A customer loss or slower qualification could reduce sales while receivables/inventory rise and suppliers require faster payment. Remaining project commitments, tax/employee claims and replacement spending must still be paid. Earmarked deposits cannot fund operating shortfalls. If planned bank funding is unavailable or deposit access delayed, an intraperiod cash breach can occur before a superficially healthy year-end balance; later forecasts do not undo missed obligations.

The bear path combines 4% growth, 15% EBITDA margin, 90-day collection, 15% inventory, narrower supplier funding, losses and a tax call. It is not a collection of unrelated independent probabilities. After a breach, recovery, restructuring, asset realization and priority claims are unknown; ordinary equity recovery is **NS**, not an attractive rebound CAGR. Equity could suffer severe permanent loss and illiquid trading could prevent exit. D 3 and P 2 reflect asymmetry and demanding expectations, not an accusation of default. The thesis-break variable is **cash available before mandatory project/operating payments under actual sanctioned funding**, followed by sustained commercial conversion of the new capacity.

An optimistic countercase deserves retention: the company has generated real cumulative CFO, historically short collections, rising existing-customer sales and physical trial-production progress; a well-funded ramp could grow into the asset base. These facts prevent calling the business proven poor. They do not establish today's funding or justify ignoring the quoted valuation.

sections.title: Fivefold and tenfold feasibility
sections.content_markdown:
**5× /10× classification: Speculative / unsupported.** Neither target has a feasible bracket in the tested base-economics funding domain.

Fivefold price appreciation requires 37.97% annual growth over five years or 17.46% over ten; tenfold requires 58.49% or 25.89%, respectively, before transaction costs. That is a shareholder-price identity, not a revenue forecast. At unchanged current shares, 5× and 10× equity values would be approximately ₹5,140.15 crore and ₹10,280.30 crore; future dilution raises the enterprise earnings burden.

The reverse tests above solve the operating revenue growth needed under the full five-/ten-year model, retaining every infeasible financing path. Separate 8/10/12/15/18/20× exit EV/EBIT grids test operating performance versus multiple effects, and a 10× lower-multiple ten-year reverse case challenges reliance on a premium exit. The capacity envelope cannot supply unlimited sales: every trial above funded capacity incurs incremental investment, working capital and reserves. A 25% or 40% long growth assumption is neither evidence of demand access nor a free scaling option. In the tested base-economics grid the largest surviving DCF price multiple is about 0.745× over five years and 1.551× over ten; the ten-year 10× EV/EBIT crosscheck reaches about 2.997×, below 5×. The largest surviving grid value is not a mathematical maximum over all possible economics. None of these tests establishes that 5×/10× is probable. Without a current funding bridge and demonstrated new-plant economics, a multibagger label would be promotional rather than analytical.

sections.title: Final classification and conditional action
sections.content_markdown:
**Hold — unresolved evidence.** BQS NS, GQS 7.1, IAS NS; no compounder designation. Missing BAL/R prevents applying the ordinary numeric matrix as if neutral values were known. The record belongs in **Pending evidence**, not at the bottom of a scored ranking and not in an investable high-growth list. This is not a governance exclusion: G1/G2/G4 are conditional and G3 is Hold, not an asserted failure.

The compounder test fails to establish current financing resilience, long-duration new-capital returns and attractive price-dependent expected return. Strong historical growth and cash conversion alone do not meet it. No unconditional entry range is supportable. Conditional model hurdle prices are useful for showing how much execution the market demands, but the first action is to obtain the actual project cash/debt bridge and commercial economics. A materially lower price could improve future R/P only after those gaps become scoreable. There is no public repository or website publication implied by this authored research artifact.
